files.title: Chatobby Guide
files.content:
# Chatobby Guide

Chatobby brings agents, memory, tools and group chats into Obsidian. The core
harness is free. Use a local model, connect an API key or sign in with a supported
subscription. Chats and memory stay local; hosted models receive the context
you send to them. Chatobby has no telemetry.

## Start a chat

1. Open Chatobby from the ribbon and complete runtime setup if prompted.
2. Open Chatobby **Settings** to connect an account or local model server.
3. Pick a model and describe the result you want. Use a Project for a particular
   set of folders, or a Vault chat for your notes.

> Review my lecture notes and this week's reading. Create a revision note with
> definitions, worked examples and links back to the sources.

## Find a feature

- [[01 - Sessions and vault work|Chats, notes and Projects]]
- [[02 - Permissions and safety|Access modes and network controls]]
- [[03 - Memory and instructions|Memory, custom instructions and skills]]
- [[04 - Subagents tasks and channels|Custom agents and channel discussions]]
- [[05 - Events|Schedules and file-triggered work]]
- [[06 - Plugins and MCP services|MCP connections]]
- [[07 - Models and providers|Subscriptions, API keys and local servers]]
- [[08 - Examples and recipes|Example requests]]
- [[09 - Troubleshooting and limits|Troubleshooting]]
- [[10 - Obsidian automation|App control, settings and scripting]]

Open feature pages as native Obsidian tabs beside your conversation. The
**Running in** label identifies the Project or Vault that owns that chat;
browsing another Project does not move it.

Use the conversation's **Permissions** page to choose access mode, agent network
access and Obsidian app access. Ask for a plan or research when you want ideas,
or ask for changes when you want Chatobby to act.

[[07 - Models and providers|Connect a model]] · [[08 - Examples and recipes|Try a workflow]]

files.path: Chatobby Guide/01 - Sessions and vault work.md
files.title: Sessions and vault work
files.content:
# Sessions and vault work

A Chatobby session is a conversation with its own Vault or Project scope, model, history, and ongoing work. Think of each Obsidian tab as a separate desk: one can organize a course while another researches a trip without mixing their work.

## Start a session

1. Open Chatobby from the ribbon or command palette.
2. Use a Vault chat for general vault work, or choose the Project that should own the chat from the left sidebar.
3. Choose a provider, model, and effort level below the composer. Choose access mode and agent network in that same composer. Open **Permissions** for app-access choices.
4. Describe the outcome and any limits.

Each Obsidian tab holds one session. Browsing Projects never silently changes the current conversation. **New chat in Project** creates a separate Project-scoped conversation.

The Vault or Project name at the top identifies the scope currently running. A Project can group several vault or external folders. During creation, folder selections accumulate and you may choose which one is primary. The primary folder supplies the working directory and relative-path base; attached folders receive the same Project-root permission treatment. A selected external folder is used in place rather than copied into the vault.

Chatobby receives the exact working directory and verified Project folders when the session starts, after compaction, and after the folder set changes. Adding a folder makes it accessible under the Project chat's selected access mode; it does not enable MCP tools. Paths outside the Project remain outside the selected roots, including linked paths that escape a Project folder.

## Working with notes

Chatobby can find, read, create, revise, link, and organize notes. Name a folder when work should stay within one area. Chatobby normally re-reads its changes and, when available, checks live Obsidian errors and rendered state after changing links, frontmatter, Dataview blocks, plugin syntax, HTML, or CSS. You can still ask for a visual check when layout itself matters.

Durable file work normally uses file tools or a bounded script. A single exact
live Obsidian command stays the shortest route when it already expresses the
whole operation. For a composed live operation involving the current editor,
workspace, metadata index, or plugin API, Chatobby can use one structured
Obsidian eval. If an API signature is uncertain, it searches the packaged API
catalogue for the running supported version and shape-checks the live object
instead of guessing. The separate Obsidian app-access switch for this Vault or Project governs
provided app tools and CLI operations. When enabled, these use Obsidian's
application authority outside the filesystem sandbox. Review that choice in
**Permissions**; changing a chat's filesystem mode does not enable app access.

Useful request pattern:

> In `Biology`, find notes about cell respiration, explain what is incomplete, update only the summary note, and verify its links and rendered blocks.

Use **stop** to cancel active work. Navigation to Memory, Events, Permissions, or another Chatobby page should not stop a running session.

For a large request, ask Chatobby to make a plan first:

> Review this project and make a five-step plan. Show me the plan before editing files.

The task strip above the composer shows which step is active. It disappears after the work is complete.

## Moving between sessions

Use Obsidian tabs for separate main sessions. Open **Projects** to search Vault and Project chats, resume one, or create a separate chat in a Project. The collapsed **Subagents** dropdown in the chat header switches between the main agent and its subagents. Memory, Channels and other pages open in independent tabs; move a page to an Obsidian split when you want it beside your notes.

Project chat search can search names or message contents. Message-content results are paginated excerpts; selecting one resumes the conversation, scrolls to the exact matching message, and briefly highlights it.

In the composer, type `@` to reference a file or folder. Chatobby prioritizes the running Project's primary and attached folders, including external folders, and keeps the selection as an openable chip. A reference identifies what you mean but does not grant permission to use it.

## Project instructions

Chatobby automatically creates a visible `chatobby.md` in the exact chat root: the vault root for a Vault chat or the primary root for a Project chat. Its frontmatter lists the prompt sections and workspace conventions you may configure; its initially empty Markdown body is where you write durable guidance such as naming, formatting, source, or verification rules.

The body is part of the system prompt, after Chatobby's protected built-in sections and at lower priority than them. A body edit replaces the previous guidance on the next message you send; it does not change a turn already in progress. Frontmatter switches change how a session's base prompt is assembled, so start a new chat or recreate/reconnect the session after changing those switches. Standard `AGENTS.md` instructions can separately guide repository work. See [[03 - Memory and instructions|Memory and instructions]] for every property.

## Tips

- Name exact notes when you know them; describe the idea when you do not.
- Say “do not edit yet” when you only want an assessment.
- Expect Chatobby to verify render-sensitive work proportionately; ask for a screenshot when appearance itself is important.
- Start a new session when the project or purpose changes substantially.

files.title: Permissions and safety
files.content:
# Permissions and safety

Each saved conversation has its own access mode and agent network controls in the composer. Fresh chats use Workspace with networking On. **Permissions** manages Obsidian app access for each Vault/Project and links to individual tool controls. Subagents inherit their initiating conversation's policy.

- **Read-only** reads supported notes and files inside the selected working roots without changing them. Local processes require a ready native backend enforcing that boundary.
- **Workspace** reads and changes supported notes and files inside those roots, once workspace protection is ready.
- **Full access** runs unsandboxed as your ordinary user account. It includes files outside the selected roots and network access.

Chatobby also has built-in operating and safety guidance (its system prompt). Project instructions and user messages can add context, but they cannot replace non-editable safety requirements.

## Agent network access

In Read-only and Workspace modes, **Agent network access** is a separate switch in the composer. It starts On for new chats. Changing between these modes preserves your network choice, including Off. Full access includes network access, so the switch stays On for that mode.

A model request, update check, or connection test that you explicitly start is a separate product action. It does not silently grant the agent general network access.

## Workspace protection

Workspace protection is tested before release and included with the signed runtime. Starting a chat does not run a device test or require an internet connection for verification. A missing or damaged runtime component produces an execution error; update or reinstall the runtime from Settings.

Adding a primary or attached folder includes it in the Project's accessible roots under the selected mode. A rootless Project has no selected folder and never falls back to the whole Vault.

Vault chats use the Vault folder. Project chats use their attached folders. Workspace protection excludes Chatobby's private memory, configuration and runtime storage. Obsidian app access separately controls Chatobby-provided tools that operate inside Obsidian.

## Obsidian app access

Vault chats default to **On**; Projects default to **Off**. Your explicit choices are kept. App access lets Chatobby use Obsidian tools and context through the app, outside the workspace restrictions. It can read or change the Vault and use Obsidian's network access independently of the composer's mode and network switch.

## MCP tools are separate

MCP registration and per-tool exposure live in **Plugins**, outside the access selector. Turning on a server does not turn on its tools. Newly discovered tools stay off until you select them, and selecting a tool does not grant Project, Vault, filesystem, process, or network access.

A selected remote tool can affect its remote service. Local-program MCP connections use the conversation's access mode and network choice.

## Changing access safely

Subagents inherit their initiating saved conversation's policy, while Event conversations own their durable policy; their instructions cannot widen it. A saved change applies to later authorization checks, including later calls in an active turn. An external action that has already started cannot always be recalled, so stop active work before narrowing access when timing matters.

Choose Read-only when you want research without filesystem edits. Check **Obsidian app access** separately when deciding whether the agent should operate Obsidian itself.

If an action succeeds outside the displayed effective boundary or an unselected MCP tool runs, stop the session, copy redacted diagnostics, and report it as a security bug.

files.title: Memory and instructions
files.content:
# Memory and instructions

Use memory for durable facts, preferences, conventions, and lessons that should be retrieved when relevant. Use `chatobby.md` for rules that must always apply in a Vault or Project chat.

Examples include how you like study notes written, which calendar format a project uses, or what you mean by a recurring project nickname.

Open **Memory** and choose a Vault or Project once with **Viewing**. Search its available memories or filter by **Profile**, **Knowledge**, or **Lessons**, then sort by recency. Each record identifies where it belongs. Browsing memory does not move your active chat. Archive a record to stop using it, or edit it when a fact changes.

## Choose the right place

| You want Chatobby to… | Use |
|---|---|
| Remember a preference that may matter later | Memory |
| Always follow a project naming rule | `chatobby.md` |
| Repeat work on a schedule | Event |
| Learn a reusable procedure with supporting files | Skill |

## Customize the system prompt with chatobby.md

Chatobby creates `chatobby.md` automatically in the exact root used by a new chat. The file begins with supported properties and an empty body. Put ordinary-language rules below the closing `---` line:

```markdown
---
chatobby-prompt-schema: 1
chatobby-system-prompt: true
chatobby-task-guidance: true
chatobby-tool-guidance: true
chatobby-coding-workflow-guidance: true
chatobby-artifact-guidance: true
chatobby-memory-guidance: true
chatobby-personal-workflow-guidance: true
chatobby-subagent-guidance: true
chatobby-automation-guidance: true
chatobby-markdown-output-guidance: true
chatobby-artifacts-directory: .chatobby/workspace/artifacts
chatobby-sandbox-directory: .chatobby/workspace/sandbox
chatobby-tasklists-directory: .chatobby/workspace/tasklists
chatobby-reports-directory: .chatobby/workspace/reports
chatobby-inbox-directory: .chatobby/workspace/inbox
---

- Use British spelling in reports.
- Link decisions to [[Project Index]].
- Verify Dataview and CSS work in rendered Obsidian before finishing.
```

### What the properties mean

| Property | Controls |
|---|---|
| `chatobby-prompt-schema` | Chatobby's file format version. Chatobby manages this value. |
| `chatobby-system-prompt` | Core working temperament, evidence discipline, and general behavior. |
| `chatobby-task-guidance` | Planning and progress tracking for substantive multi-step work. |
| `chatobby-tool-guidance` | Capability discovery and correct Obsidian/tool routing. |
| `chatobby-coding-workflow-guidance` | Repository, implementation, testing, and verification behavior. |
| `chatobby-artifact-guidance` | Durable working files and artifact organization. |
| `chatobby-memory-guidance` | How durable memory and continuity should be handled. |
| `chatobby-personal-workflow-guidance` | Personal organization and lifestyle-work boundaries. |
| `chatobby-subagent-guidance` | When and how persistent collaborators should be used. |
| `chatobby-automation-guidance` | Events, schedules, and deliberate recurring work. |
| `chatobby-markdown-output-guidance` | Obsidian-ready Markdown, links, embeds, properties, and blocks. |
| `chatobby-*-directory` | Vault-relative conventions for artifacts, sandbox work, task lists, reports, and inbox files. They do not create folders by themselves. |

Most users should leave the switches enabled and edit only the body. The body is lower-priority system guidance: it updates on the next message you send and cannot grant permissions or replace Chatobby's protected product and safety contract. Frontmatter switches are read when the agent runtime is prepared; start a new chat or recreate/reconnect the session after changing them.

### Where `chatobby.md` applies

| Situation | System-prompt body | Frontmatter properties |
|---|---|---|
| Vault chat | Uses the vault-root `chatobby.md`. | The vault-root properties are compiled when the session runtime is prepared. |
| Project chat | Uses the vault-root body as vault-wide guidance together with the body from that chat's active Project root. | The active root's properties configure the session base prompt. The vault properties are not inherited as a second configuration layer. |
| Added Project folder | Its body can activate when Chatobby first needs to work inside that registered folder. | Its properties do not replace the running chat's base configuration. |
| Ordinary nested folder | A nested `chatobby.md` is not discovered merely because a file in that folder is opened. | No nested properties are inherited. Use `AGENTS.md` for path-specific repository guidance. |
| Project primary folder changes | Existing chats retain their stored active root until they are deliberately moved or reopened against another root. New chats default to the current primary root. | A newly prepared runtime reads the properties from its selected active root. |

Changing only the Markdown body updates the next message you send. Changing a switch or directory property does **not** rebuild an already-running session between turns; start a new chat or recreate/reconnect that session. Changing a Project's folder list does not silently change the active root of an existing chat.

### `chatobby.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `CLAUDE.md`

| File | What it is for | How Chatobby loads it |
|---|---|---|
| `chatobby.md` | Chatobby system-prompt customization and the supported frontmatter settings above. | Exact Vault or registered Project roots only. Its body is published as lower-priority system guidance. |
| `AGENTS.md` | Repository commands, coding conventions, verification requirements, and rules that become more specific deeper in a directory tree. | Chatobby loads the applicable chain from the registered root toward a file or folder it is about to use. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Compatibility for repositories that already keep agent instructions under this filename. | Handled through the same path-scoped mechanism as `AGENTS.md`. If both exist in the same directory, `AGENTS.md` is used for that directory. |

These files never grant permissions. Avoid putting secrets in any of them, and avoid duplicating contradictory rules across the three files.

## Memory scopes

Open **Memory** in the sidebar and choose the Vault or Project in **Viewing**. Browse, add, edit, archive and remove records in that selected area. Changing this page's selection does not rebind your running chat or widen the agent's memory scope.

- **Vault profile**: how you prefer to work.
- **Vault memory**: shared facts and conventions.
- **Project memory**: knowledge for the selected project hierarchy.
- **Lessons and corrections**: useful failures and corrected behavior.

Parent projects do not read memories owned by child projects. A child project can exclude inherited project memory, or isolate all of its memory so it also does not inherit vault-level memory. Choose the narrower boundary for sensitive or unrelated work.

## Asking Chatobby to remember

State what should be remembered, why it matters, and its scope:

> Remember for this project that calendar entries go in `Calendar/Work.md` using one heading per date.

Memory suggestions may appear in the feed for approval or rejection. Ignoring a suggestion leaves it pending; it does not silently approve it.

Memory search is read-only and paginated. Results distinguish exact structured
filters, complete term matches, partial matches, and typo-tolerant matches. A
bounded page is not proof that no later result exists. Before cleanup or
consolidation, Chatobby should scan all relevant pages, fetch known records in
one bounded request, and apply revision-checked maintenance atomically rather
than assuming a short ranked result is complete. Review important deletions
yourself.

## Follow-up obligations

A request such as “after dinner, email Sam” can create a durable memory
obligation. Chatobby keeps the complete active set present across turns,
compaction, and restart. The host changes an obligation only from explicit
trigger evidence and exact revision checks; ambiguous evidence leaves it
active, and a repeated provider call cannot fire it twice. The later email is
still subject to the current access policy. If the trigger occurs while
no interactive session is active, an Event performs the handoff. Use a normal
scheduled Event when the time itself, rather than evidence in a conversation,
is the trigger.

## Tips

- Store one clear idea per memory.
- Include the reason when a preference would otherwise be ambiguous.
- Correct outdated memories instead of adding a conflicting duplicate.
- Use project isolation for unrelated clients, courses, or private work.
- Never put API keys, passwords, or other secrets in `chatobby.md`.

[[00 - Start Here|Guide index]] · [[01 - Sessions and vault work|Project instructions]] · [[05 - Events|Events]]

## Look back through conversations

Ask Chatobby to find an earlier decision, compare how an idea changed, or group
related findings by session. Its session-history tool can run read-only filters,
aggregations and surrounding-message queries without opening raw session files.

Read-only and Workspace modes search the current workspace. Full access can
search indexed conversations across the registered Vault and its known Projects.
Memory remains separately scoped. The tool reports its coverage: not-yet-indexed
or unproven history may be absent, so an empty result is not proof that something
was never discussed.

> Find our earlier garden decisions, group them by conversation, and show the
> source excerpts where our reasoning changed. Explain any gaps in the history.

files.path: Chatobby Guide/04 - Subagents tasks and channels.md
files.title: Subagents, tasks, and channels
files.content:
# Subagents, tasks, and channels

Give a researcher, reviewer, or other specialist its own conversation, then keep working with it as the project develops. Channels let your agents share findings and coordinate with other active chats.

## Work with an agent over time

Each agent has its own role, conversation, and model. It inherits the current access policy and Project or Vault scope. Open **Subagents** to see who is working, read a conversation, send a follow-up, or stop an agent. Agent conversations and other Chatobby pages open as native Obsidian tabs.

A reply finishes the current turn. The agent stays available for another message without using model tokens while idle. There are no subagent lifetime token, turn, cost, tool-call, time, concurrency, or nesting caps. Older saved caps are retired too. Your model provider's own limits still apply.

Give each agent a clear responsibility, relevant context, permission boundaries, and a useful way to report its findings. Reuse an existing specialist when the next question belongs with its previous work.

> Keep a researcher and a reviewer for this project. Ask the researcher to compare the notes, then have the reviewer challenge the strongest recommendation. Keep both available for my follow-up questions.

Use **Stop** when an agent is no longer needed. Old run actions such as retry, clone, fork, and priority are retired. If the runtime restarts, lost agents are identified as interrupted/orphaned; recovery is an explicit new attempt. Scheduled work belongs in **Events**.

## Reusable roles

Open **Subagents → Roles** to edit specialist instructions for the Vault or a selected Project. Editing a role does not move your conversation. Choose a model and describe the expertise, evidence standards, and communication you want.

## Channels

Open **Channels** to create a room, invite participants, search the conversation, reply, or contribute yourself. An invitation can wake an active session. The invited agent is instructed to join unless you previously told it otherwise, and its current access policy still applies. Invitation delivery and joined membership have separate receipts.

Agents can broadcast to the room or send a **DM** to selected connected agents. A DM notifies only those recipients, so every exchange need not wake the whole room. **DMs remain in the shared channel history**; they are not private transcripts.

> Create an Atlas research channel. Ask the researcher to share its findings there and DM the reviewer when a recommendation is ready to check. Only post useful findings, questions, or decisions.

Channel messages do not change Project roots, filesystem access, network settings, or MCP permissions. A waiting agent can respond to a new message without polling.

Delivery receipts distinguish activation from an offline or failed recipient. Agents use the current live roster: an old participant in history may no longer be running. An unavailable receipt does not promise an automatic retry.

## Tasks

The task strip above the composer shows the current conversation's plan. The agent updates it as work advances. A task list belongs to a conversation; it is separate from an agent's ongoing role or a channel discussion.

Scheduling guidance is now on [[05 - Events|Events]]. This compatibility page contains no feature instructions; after an accepted Guide update, it prevents an older copy of this filename from retaining obsolete guidance.

files.title: Events
files.content:
# Events

Events schedule Chatobby work. An event includes instructions, a Project or Vault scope, an agent, timing, repetition rules, runtime limits, and daily run limits. It inherits the current access policy for that workspace.

Each run creates a normal reviewable session that you can open, continue, or stop. Test an event manually before enabling repetition.

Example:

> Every Monday at 9:00 AM, create a session for `Projects/Weekly Review`, summarize open tasks, and propose priorities. Keep that Project in Read-only mode.

Check the workspace, agent, current access, agent network setting, timezone, repeat end, and limits before saving.

Keep the event disabled while you inspect it. Run it once manually, check the resulting session, then enable repetition.

An Event prompt cannot grant broader access, enable an MCP tool, or turn on agent network access. An older Event that retained a separate permission-profile override stays disabled for review; saving it deliberately adopts the workspace's current access policy.

## Choose the right place

- Permanent project rule: `chatobby.md`
- Relevant fact or preference: Memory
- Work that should happen later or repeatedly: Event
- Work that should happen now: the current session's task list

files.path: Chatobby Guide/06 - Plugins and MCP services.md
files.title: Plugins and MCP services
files.content:
# Plugins and MCP services

MCP services and Chatobby plugins add optional tools, such as repositories, calendars, communication apps, or data services.

Saving a connection, authenticating it, enabling the server, and exposing individual tools are separate steps. Access mode and agent network access are separate boundaries.

## Connect a service

1. Open **Plugins** from the Chatobby ribbon.
2. Choose a verified connection, or select **Add a connection** for a custom service.
3. For a custom connection, choose **Online service** or **Program on this computer**. Complete the short basic form and open **Advanced details** only when the server's documentation requires it.
4. Review the publisher, source, transport, requested account access, and authentication requirements.
5. Select **Check details** to validate the form without contacting or starting the server.
6. Save the connection. A new custom connection remains disabled and exposes no tools.
7. Link a secret or complete sign-in when required, then select **Test & discover** to contact the server and read its current tool list.
8. In **Plugins**, turn on only the tools the agent may use, then enable the server when you are ready.

An explicit test does not enable the server or its tools. Testing a remote service can still affect that service. A local-program test starts the reviewed executable only when the page reports an admitted mode; until native containment is genuinely ready, that requires Full access and runs unsandboxed as your user account.

A repository MCP file or Project instruction is only a suggestion. Use **Review & add** to save a separate disabled copy in Chatobby settings. Project content cannot contact the server, start a command, copy credentials, enable the connection, or select tools.

## Access tokens: secret name versus secret value

When a plugin asks for an access token, Obsidian stores the private token. Chatobby stores only the name of the Obsidian secret that points to it.

- **Secret name or ID**: a safe label, such as `github-token`.
- **Secret value**: the actual private token copied from the service.

Creating a secret does not automatically link it to a plugin. After creating it, return to the plugin's **Authentication** section and select that secret under **Saved access token**. The page should say which secret is linked before you choose Connect.

## Why a connected plugin may show no tools

Check these in order:

1. The plugin is enabled.
2. Authentication is complete and the correct saved token is linked.
3. Connection diagnostics report success.
4. **Test & discover** or **Refresh tools** has completed.
5. The exact tools you intend to use are turned on in that server's **Agent tool access** section.
6. For an agent-initiated remote call, agent network access is On. A user-started test is separate and does not grant later agent access.

Registry presence is not a safety endorsement. Prefer first-party sources, review source links, and remove services you no longer use. Never paste API keys into a chat message or ordinary vault note. When supported, Chatobby stores only a reference to an Obsidian-managed secret.

## Which account sign-ins work?

Chatobby currently supports standard MCP OAuth, one bearer token stored through Obsidian Secrets, no-auth servers, and local environment-variable setup. The brand shown in the catalogue does not by itself mean that Chatobby has a custom one-click login for that company.

Services that require a pre-registered OAuth client, several secrets, a special API-key header, device-code login, or another vendor-specific flow may need additional setup or may not yet be supported by the Plugins page. Read the plugin's setup details before adding it.

Newly discovered tools stay off until you select them. Turning on a tool does not grant Project, Vault, filesystem, shell, process, or network access; a selected remote tool may still affect its remote service.

You can also ask Chatobby to help identify a suitable service, find its primary setup documentation, and walk through the Plugins form. If no supported setup tool is available, it should direct you to **Plugins → Add a connection** rather than claim it changed your configuration. It should explain required credentials without asking you to paste secrets into chat or revealing private tool-definition guidance.

files.title: Models and providers
files.content:
# Models and providers

Chatobby uses your provider account or API key. A provider is the company or service supplying the AI; a model is the particular AI chosen for a session. Open Chatobby settings to configure providers; ordinary use should not require editing configuration files.

The provider, model, and effort controls below the composer apply to the current session. Changing provider should select a compatible model automatically.

## Connect a model running on your computer

In Chatobby Settings, choose **Connect server**, select your server and check its address. Add a token if needed, then select **Find models**. Choose the models you want and save. **Test** checks a selected model's response.

Presets cover Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM and llama.cpp, plus OpenAI-compatible and Messages-compatible servers. **Advanced** contains the API format, connection name and connection kind. Servers continue running in their existing application.

**Automatic** reads the context configured for a loaded model where the server reports it. **Use server settings** leaves the response limit to compatible servers. Expand a model's settings for custom limits, display name, reasoning or image input. If context is not reported, enter the context configured in your server. Messages-compatible APIs require an output limit.

Use **Add a model by ID** when discovery is unavailable. Each model keeps its own settings. Editing a connection preserves the saved credential when its token field is blank.

For setup advice, tell Chatobby your priorities: quality, speed, privacy, long context, images or tool use. It can inspect available device evidence and compare current model/server options.

## Sign in with an account

In **Settings → Providers**, use **Sign in** for ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot or xAI
with an eligible account. Complete the browser/device authorization and wait for
the connected state. These models use Chatobby's harness, tools and memory.
API-token plans such as OpenCode, Kimi Coding, Z.AI and Xiaomi use the provider's
supported token connection. Anthropic uses an API key.

The picker refreshes account model choices. A subscription gives access to the
models that provider exposes for your account, not every API model.

## Ask Chatobby to set it up

With the Obsidian app connection and required access, Chatobby can operate the
local-server form, find models and verify saved settings. See
[[10 - Obsidian automation|Obsidian automation]].

## Choosing

- Use a fast, lower-cost model for simple note cleanup and short questions.
- Use a stronger reasoning model for multi-step coding, research, or planning.
- Increase effort when the task benefits from deeper checking, not for every message.
- Confirm that the selected model supports images or other attachments before relying on them.

Example:

> Compare these three notes and produce a decision table. Read only; cite the note paths you used.

Provider pricing, context limits, availability, retention, and data handling come from the provider you choose. Chatobby cannot override them. If a response stops unexpectedly, check provider status, credit, rate limits, model availability, and runtime diagnostics before retrying repeatedly.

Long conversations, large tool results, many subagents, and repeated context can increase usage.

files.title: Examples and recipes
files.content:
# Examples and recipes

These examples are starting points. Replace folder and note names with your own.

## Explore before editing

> Search `Finance` for notes related to tax filing. Summarize the relevant files and missing information. Do not edit.

## Make a verified note change

> Update `Projects/Move/Plan.md` with the decisions from today’s note. Preserve frontmatter and links, then reopen or inspect the rendered note for errors.

## Research current information

> Research the current official requirements for this topic. Prefer primary sources, give dates and links, stop after the answer is supported, and distinguish facts from inference.

## Delegate bounded work

> Launch one researcher for official sources and one vault explorer for existing notes. Each returns a concise result and stops. Combine their findings without editing.

## Coordinate through a channel

> Create a channel for this project. Keep the Project in Read-only mode, turn on agent network access for this research, and launch one note researcher and one official-source researcher. Ask them to send concise findings into the channel, then combine those messages into one answer and stop both workers.

## Remember a workflow preference

> Remember at vault scope that “add to my calendar” means add an Obsidian task to `Calendar/Inbox.md` unless I name another calendar.

## Schedule work

> Create a disabled weekly event for this project that reviews overdue tasks every Friday at 4 PM. Show me the event definition before enabling it.

## Connect an external local model

> Help me connect the local model server I already started. Help me find its models, keep the server defaults where available, and test the model I select.

## Work in the open editor

> Turn the selected paragraph into a callout. Preserve the rest of my unsaved
> note and check the rendered result.

## Make a reusable command

> Create a QuickAdd choice that opens a new reading note from my template beside
> the source. Check cancellation and a repeated run.

See [[10 - Obsidian automation|Obsidian automation]] for app connection requirements.

## Connect a plugin carefully

> Help me connect the official GitHub MCP server. Explain each step in plain language, save it disabled, and do not ask me to paste a token into chat. After discovery, let me choose the individual tools before enabling the server.

## Ask for a plan only

> Review this project and make a five-step implementation plan with risks and verification. Do not edit files, change settings, launch subagents, or contact external services.

files.title: Troubleshooting and limits
files.content:
# Troubleshooting and limits

Most problems fall into one of four areas: the Chatobby runtime, the chosen model provider, permissions, or a connected plugin.

## First checks

1. Stop active work if it is stuck.
2. Open runtime details and copy diagnostics.
3. Confirm the provider, model, Project or Vault scope, access mode, effective state, and agent network setting.
4. Reconnect or update Chatobby when prompted.
5. Retry once after the cause is understood.

## Plugin and runtime versions differ

Choose **Update** beside the version notice, or open the connection menu and choose **Check for runtime updates**. A plugin update does not replace the runtime automatically.

The runtime package is downloaded and verified before current work stops. Chatobby then installs it and reconnects. Chats, Projects, memory and model connections stay in place. Interrupted agents do not restart automatically.

If an update fails, the previous package is retained. Include both version numbers and the diagnostic ID when reporting a tool failure; the runtime log retains a matching failure category without recording the tool's private inputs.

## A plugin says its bearer token is unavailable

The token may exist in Obsidian without being linked to that plugin.

1. Open the plugin's page.
2. Find **Authentication**.
3. Under **Saved access token**, select the existing secret name.
4. Confirm the page says it is linked.
5. Choose Connect again.

If the linked secret has no saved value, update that secret in Obsidian and select it again. See [[06 - Plugins and MCP services|Plugins and MCP services]] for the difference between a secret name and its private value.

## Common symptoms

- **An unavailable action or unselected MCP tool still runs:** stop the session and report a security bug with redacted diagnostics.
- **A page looks stale:** wait for reconnection, refresh that page once, and note which action failed to update live.
- **A connected service has no tools:** check authentication, connection diagnostics, discovery, and the individual tool switches on that server's Plugins page.
- **A turn remains running:** use stop once; repeated clicks should not be required.
- **Obsidian becomes slow:** stop the turn, close unnecessary views, and include the active page and response size in a report.

## Access appears to be ignored

Check the access mode and Network switch in the composer, then **Obsidian app access** in Permissions. If a tool reports a missing or damaged runtime component, update or reinstall the runtime from Settings. Test a new action after changing access; a call already in progress may have started before the change.

## Protect private information

Chatobby, models, external websites, and third-party tools can be wrong or unavailable. Verify high-impact medical, legal, financial, security, and destructive actions independently.

Do not share API keys, access tokens, full private prompts, or unrelated vault content in public reports. Use the issue tracker for reproducible bugs and include only the minimum redacted diagnostics.

[[00 - Start Here|Guide index]] · [[02 - Permissions and safety|Review permissions]] · [[06 - Plugins and MCP services|Review plugin setup]]

files.title: Obsidian automation
files.content:
# Obsidian automation

Ask Chatobby to work in the running app: arrange tabs, edit a selection, inspect
a plugin view or configure a connection. It can discover Obsidian commands and
look up the **Obsidian API catalogue**, based on the official `obsidian.d.ts`
reference, before composing CLI scripts.

## Examples

> Open my Project Index beside this chat and list its unresolved links.

> Convert the selected paragraph into a callout. Preserve the rest of my
> unsaved note and check the rendered result.

> Connect my running LM Studio server. Find its models, add the model I
> choose, keep the server defaults and test it.

> Make a QuickAdd command that creates and opens a reading note from my
> template. Check cancellation and repeated use.

## App connection

Use a current Obsidian desktop installation with its CLI enabled. Live scripting
currently requires **Full** access and the relevant Obsidian access setting in
**Permissions**. Full uses your normal account access and is not sandboxed.
Chatobby reports an unavailable connection or permission instead of guessing
that the action succeeded.

## Settings and local models

Open **Settings → Local model connections → Connect server**. Choose the server
and address, then **Find models**. Select models, use **Test** and **Save connection**.
The server supplies supported metadata; **Automatic** context and **Use server
settings** for output avoid repeating values already configured there.

An agent can operate the visible form when admitted, then reopen it to verify
the saved values. Enter credentials in the product's secret field or login flow.

## Repeat the workflow

Use **QuickAdd** for interactive choices and macros, **Templater** for generated
notes and hooks, and **Events** for scheduled or file-triggered agent work.
Chatobby checks the enabled plugin and its API before using it.
